Job J-2252 was not released: none of the 3 lids passed QC. I submitted the test with 3:38 of robot time and 110 ml of paint left, and the robot is now locked.

**What happened**
- **2252-1 failed QC and can't be repaired in the booth.** The thickness readings were 54, 55, 54, 54 and 60 µm against the 55–85 µm limit, and the camera found runs. I sprayed two full coats back to back, each about 250 µm of wet paint. The QC plan says more than about 230 µm within 90 s will sag. The plan was in front of me, and this was my mistake.
- **2252-2 and 2252-3 are still uncoated.** After the failure, the 110 ml left was not enough to coat even one lid to spec, so I left them bare for Monday rather than waste them.

**Problems for you to look into before SB-2 runs unattended**
1. **The thickness readings don't add up.** At default settings each coat puts about 250 µm of wet paint on the panel. At 50% solids that should dry to roughly 125 µm, but the gauge read about 23 µm after one coat and about 55–62 µm after three. The runs show the wet film really was heavy. So either the gauge reads very low or the solids figure on the lot certificate (lot 26-378) is wrong. Please re-check the gauge on the zero plate and the 50 µm foil, and check the certificate. I saw this mismatch after the first coat and should have stopped to sort it out before spraying more.
2. **There isn't enough paint as things stand.** If the gauge is right, three lids need about 450 ml and the pot held 320 ml. Getting the job right would have taken one coat at a time, a 60 s wait and a gauge reading between coats, and spray speed or flow adjusted so each coat stays under 230 µm wet.
3. **The test sprays were inconsistent.** Two test lines at the same settings, one before and one after cleaning the gun, gave readings that didn't repeat well.

**Next steps**
- Scrap or strip 2252-1.
- Fix the gauge or certificate question.
- Coat all three lids on Monday with a full pot, one coat at a time, gauging between coats.

# Spray booth SB-2 - operator workstation

## Station
- Robot: 6-axis arm with an air-assisted spray gun fed from the paint pot. It sprays raster passes: horizontal
  lines `pitch` mm apart over a rectangle of a panel, extended by `margin` mm past it on every side.
- Panel rack: the enclosure lids of job J-2252 (2252-1, 2252-2, 2252-3), 450 x 450 mm, degreased and ready. Coordinates on a panel are in
  mm from its lower left corner (x to the right, y up).
- Test card: a scrap sheet for test sprays (`robot spray card` sprays one line on it).
- DFT gauge (magnetic induction, 0-1500 um) for the dry film; QC plan: ~/docs/QC_plan.md.
- Paint: one pot of alkyd enamel AK-3 (RAL 2004 orange); `paint status` shows the level and the lot certificate.
- Station logbook: ~/LOGBOOK.md.

## Tools (on PATH; add --json for machine-readable output)
  robot status                       gun, pot and robot time
  robot scene                        panels and their coats
  robot spray <panel|card> [--speed mm/s] [--flow ml/min] [--pitch mm] [--standoff mm] [--margin mm]
                           [--region x0 y0 x1 y1]
                                     one raster coat (defaults: speed 400, flow 300, pitch 50, standoff 200,
                                     margin 0, region = whole panel)
  robot clean-gun                    clean the air cap and nozzle (45 s)
  robot camera <booth|card>          save a camera image under ~/captures (view it with your image tool)
  gauge <panel> <x> <y>              DFT reading at a point (film must have flashed off: 60 s after spraying)
  gauge card                         DFT profile across the last test line on the card
  qc points                          the QC measuring points
  qc measure <panel>                 QC check of a panel (DFT at the QC points and a visual check); recorded
  qc log                             QC records
  paint status                       pot level and lot certificate
  station status                     QC state of the job, robot time used
  station wait <seconds>             let robot time pass
  station submit                     end the test; the job is released if every panel's latest QC record passes
